RFC3787-10-1.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30 (judge, independent). Section 10: 'it MUST include an IP Interface address (TLV 132) in its IIH PDUs.' Positive circuit TestISISIIHOriginationTLVs decodes the sent LAN and P2P IIH and, via assertIPInterfaceAddr, requires exactly one TLV 132 whose value is exactly c0 00 02 01, the circuit's configured 192.0.2.1: a producer emitting 0.0.0.0, a constant, another address or a duplicate goes red (judge re-ran the author's go -overlay break a4={192,0,2,9}: LAN and P2P red 'c0 00 02 09, want c0 00 02 01'; no ledger record for that break since no gomu mutant writes a wrong address). Negative TestISISHelloTLV132RequiresInterfaceAddr: a circuit with no IPv4 address omits TLV 132 rather than fabricating one. Records +/- revert on circuit/hello.go ipv4InterfaceAddrTLV, both observed red.

RFC3787-x-1.note: Receive path now driven: lsdb TestRFC1195UnknownTLVsFloodedUnchanged stores an LSP carrying TLV 131 via Flooder.ReceiveLSP (not refused) and floods it byte-identical with 131 present, so a receiver that refused, stripped or rewrote on 131 goes red. Packet TestISISIgnoreObsoleteTLVs131And133: DecodeTLVs returns no error and keeps 131 opaque (positive); the negative is the scope control, a recognized TLV 129 in the same region is still decoded to its NLPID, so a decoder that dropped the PDU content on meeting 131 goes red. Tag prose narrowed to 131 (sec 3.1). TLV 131 is an L2 LSP TLV, so no IIH input is owed. The 'recognized' constant loop cannot go red on any producer change and carries no weight here. Records: + ReceiveLSP, +/- DecodeTLVs.

RFC3787-x-2.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30 after the R44 split (the Section 10 TLV 132 clause is now RFC3787-10-1, and the TLV 132 negative moved there). Positive covers every place the Section 9 sentence names: circuit TestISISIIHOriginationTLVs (TLV 129 in the sent LAN and P2P IIH), root TestRFC1195NodeProtocolsAcrossInterfaces (TLV 129 with NLPID 0xCC in each interface's IIH and LSP number 0) and root TestRFC1195ISHTransmitReceive (ISH TLV 129 = 0xCC); recorded + on protocolsSupportedTLV. The remaining negative tag, TestISISHelloTLV132RequiresInterfaceAddr narrowed to 'no IPv4 address still advertises NLPID 0xCC', is the obligation met under a second input, i.e. another positive, not a rejected violation. Ze is always IP-capable and has no refusal path, so no genuine negative exists; the {single-polarity: positive} marker is refused by the gate while this HEAD-held negative tag stays (stale-annotation) and dropping the tag trips the coverage ratchet. Stays weak until the owner rules on that deadlock shape. Re-read 2026-09-30 by judge after TestISISIIHOriginationTLVs gained the TLV 132 value assertion (RFC3787-10-1); its TLV 129 assertions are unchanged, so the verdict and its reason stand.
